title: Tony Thompson (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: Anthony Theodore Thompson, born 15 November 1954, New York City; died 12 November 2003, Los Angeles, of renal cell carcinoma. Raised in Springfield Gardens, Queens; his mother Trinidadian, his father of Antiguan descent. Took up the drums after rock drummers: Ringo Starr, Mitch Mitchell, Ginger Baker, John Bonham, later Steve Gadd and Billy Cobham. Drummed for Labelle, briefly in Ecstasy, Passion & Pain, then Chic; with Chic on Sister Sledge's We Are Family and Diana Ross's Upside Down. After Chic (1983) on Rodgers's and Edwards's productions: Madonna's Like a Virgin (Like a Virgin, Material Girl, Love Don't Live Here Anymore, Shoo-Bee-Doo), Bowie's Let's Dance and the Serious Moonlight tour, Robert Palmer's Riptide (Hyperactive, Addicted to Love, I Didn't Mean to Turn You On, Riptide), Rod Stewart's Out of Order, Mick Jagger's Hard Woman. The Power Station (1985, 1996's Living in Fear); Live Aid with the Power Station and with Led Zeppelin, beside Phil Collins; the Zeppelin reunion rehearsals that followed, cut short by a car crash. Distance, Crown of Thorns, Nine Inch Nails' The Fragile.

title: Billy Amendola, 'Tony Thompson', Modern Drummer (online), 20 July 2005 (an interview from 2002)
notes: On the Power Station sound: 'a brand-new Yamaha kit (which I still play) in a very live, brick, recording studio in London ... I hit the drums very hard. That's it!' 'Samples weren't even around back then.' Addicted to Love at Compass Point: 'the first time anyone ever spent time to get a drum sound like that'; Jason Corsaro's tunnel from the bass drum up the stairs; 'what am I playing? A simple, Boom-Bop-Tish-Bop-Boom-Bop.' Let's Dance 'recorded the same way'. 'My major influences as a kid were Ginger Baker and John Bonham.' Zeppelin at Live Aid: Rock and Roll 'more like a Texas shuffle'. Tony Williams an idol; British drummers and Williams 'played more behind the beat. I noticed American drummers were more on top.' 'The reason I play drums is people like Ringo and The Beatles, Mitch Mitchell and Jimi Hendrix, Ginger Baker and Cream. John Bonham and Led Zeppelin blew me away.' Into fusion before Chic; saw Billy Cobham ('and saw God') and Steve Gadd with Chick Corea. Narada Michael Walden 'became my drum teacher and friend', taught by playing keyboards while he drummed; 'He also taught Omar Hakim.' Chic 'actually started as a rock band'. Nile Rodgers thought he played too much; Bernard Edwards: 'Just keep a bass drum, snare, and hi-hat. When you master that, then maybe I'll add another cymbal or drum.' 'It's amazing how creative you get from boredom.' The Fragile: 'all acoustic drums', 'I dig playing with sequences and loops.'

title: Richard Buskin, 'Classic Tracks: Chic, Le Freak', Sound On Sound, April 2005
notes: Engineer Bob Clearmountain, at the Power Station, New York. Rodgers: 'The rhythm track was always played completely live, without a click track, and we'd select one particular take'; no song compiled from different takes. The line-up on Le Freak: Rodgers, Edwards, Tony Thompson on drums, Rob Sabino, Raymond Jones or Andy Schwartz, the Chic Strings, Alfa Anderson and Diva Gray. The echo on the bass drum after 'Aaaaahh, freak out!' from overloading the live echo chamber, the Power Station's bathroom. On Let's Dance: 'that's Omar Hakim playing on "Modern Love". Tony Thompson is playing in the video because he was on tour with Bowie.'

title: Chic (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Nile Rodgers, Bernard Edwards and Tony Thompson the band's core; Thompson and Edwards on the Power Station's 1985 album and on Palmer's Riptide, both produced by Edwards. Inducted into the Dance Music Hall of Fame, 19 September 2005.

title: Le Freak - Wikipedia
notes: From C'est Chic (August 1978); the single September 1978. Written after the band were turned away at Studio 54 on New Year's Eve 1977. Personnel: Tony Thompson, drums.

title: Good Times (Chic song) - Wikipedia
notes: From Risqué (1979); the single June 1979. Its bass line under the Sugarhill Gang's Rapper's Delight and Queen's Another One Bites the Dust. Drums: Tony Thompson.

title: We Are Family (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Sister Sledge, January 1979, written and produced by Bernard Edwards and Nile Rodgers with Chic as the band. Personnel: Tony Thompson, drums.

title: Diana (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Diana Ross, May 1980, produced by Bernard Edwards and Nile Rodgers. Personnel: Tony Thompson, drums. Upside Down a US number one.

title: Like a Virgin (song) - Wikipedia; Like a Virgin (album) - Wikipedia
notes: The album recorded at the Power Station, New York, April 1984, produced by Nile Rodgers; released 12 November 1984. The album's credits put Tony Thompson on drums on tracks 1, 3, 5 and 7; the song's personnel: Tony Thompson, drums; Bernard Edwards, bass.

title: The Power Station (album) - Wikipedia; The Power Station (band) - Wikipedia
notes: A supergroup of Robert Palmer, Tony Thompson and Andy and John Taylor of Duran Duran, produced by Bernard Edwards, released 1985. Get It On (Bang a Gong), T. Rex's song, and Some Like It Hot the singles. Palmer left before the tour to make Riptide. Live Aid, 13 July 1985: the Power Station's set, and Thompson with Led Zeppelin, sharing the drums with Phil Collins.

title: Riptide (album) - Wikipedia; Addicted to Love (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Robert Palmer, 4 November 1985, recorded at Compass Point, Nassau, produced by Bernard Edwards. Tony Thompson, drums on tracks 1 to 4, 6, 7 and 9; Dony Wynn on 5 and 8. Addicted to Love the third song, a US number one in 1986: 'The song's drum intro is by Tony Thompson'; Edwards on bass, Eddie Martinez the guitar solo.

title: Chic, 'Le Freak', Musikladen (Radio Bremen), 1979, YouTube sywMVfEn-E0 ('Super CHIC 1979 - Le Freak')
